replacement: 26. Or does the whole of modern history, perhaps, show more confidence in life and in its ideals? Its loftiest pretension today is to be a mirror. It rejects all teleology and wants no more "proving." It disdains to play the judge, and shows its good taste in that. It asserts as little as it denies; it fixes, it "describes." All this is ascetic to a high degree, yet nihilistic to a much higher degree; make no mistake about this! In the historian you see a gloomy, hard, but determined gaze, the eye of an isolated North Pole explorer (perhaps so as not to look within, so as not to look back?). There is snow; life is silenced here; the last crows that caw here are called "whither?", "Vanity," "Nada." Nothing more flourishes or grows here, except at most the metapolitics of St. Petersburg and the "pity" of Tolstoi. Then there is that other school of historians, a perhaps still more "modern" school, voluptuous and lascivious, which ogles life and the ascetic ideal with equal fervor, which wears the word "artist" like a glove, and has by now secured a "corner" for itself in all the praise of contemplation. Oh, what a thirst these sweet intellectuals arouse, even for ascetics and winter landscapes! Nay! The devil take these "contemplative" folk! I would much rather wander with those historical Nihilists through the gloomiest, grey, cold mist! Nay, I shall not mind listening (supposing I have to choose) to someone completely unhistorical and anti-historical (a man like Dühring, for instance, whose periods have intoxicated a hitherto shy and unavowed species of "beautiful souls" in contemporary Germany, the species anarchistica within the educated proletariate). The "contemplative" are a hundred times worse. Nothing has ever made me so intensely nauseous as one of those "objective" chairs, one of those scented mannikins-about-town of history, a thing half-priest, half-satyr (Renan parfum). The high, shrill falsetto of his applause betrays what he lacks and where he lacks it: it betrays where the Fates, in his case, have plied their ghastly shears, alas! in too surgeon-like a fashion! I find this distasteful, and it tries my patience. Let him stay patient at such sights who has nothing to lose by it. For me the sight is enraging; such spectators embitter me against the "play," even more than the play itself does (history itself, you understand). Anacreontic moods come over me imperceptibly. This Nature, who gave the steer its horn and the lion its χάσμ ὀδοντων: for what purpose did Nature give me my foot? — To kick, by St. Anacreon, and not merely to run away! To trample on all the worm-eaten "chairs," the cowardly contemplators, the lascivious eunuchs of history, the flirters with ascetic ideals, the righteous hypocrites of impotence! All reverence from me to the ascetic ideal, in so far as it is honorable! So long as it believes in itself and plays no pranks on us! But I do not like all these coquettish bugs, whose insatiable ambition is to smell of the infinite until at last the infinite smells of bugs. I do not like the whited sepulchres with their stagey imitation of life. I do not like the tired and the used up who wrap themselves in wisdom and look "objective." I do not like the agitators dressed up as heroes, who hide their dummy-heads behind the stalking-horse of an ideal. I do not like the ambitious artists who would fain play the ascetic and the priest, and are at bottom nothing but tragic clowns. I do not like, again, these newest speculators in idealism, the Anti-Semites, who roll their eyes in the patent Christian-Aryan-man-of-honor fashion today, and with moralist attitudes and agitation dodges so cheap that they exhaust any patience, try to rouse all the blockhead elements in the populace (the unfailing success of every kind of intellectual charlatanism in present-day Germany is tied to the almost indisputable and already quite palpable desolation of the German mind. I look for its cause in a too exclusive diet of papers, politics, beer and Wagnerian music, not forgetting the condition this diet presupposes: the national exclusiveness and vanity, the strong but narrow principle "Germany, Germany above everything," and finally the paralysis agitans of "modern ideas"). Europe today is above all wealthy and ingenious in means of excitement; it apparently has no more pressing need than stimulantia and alcohol. Hence the enormous counterfeiting of ideals, those most fiery spirits of the mind; hence also the repulsive, evil-smelling, perjured, pseudo-alcoholic air everywhere. I should like to know how many cargoes of imitation idealism, of hero-costumes and high-falutin' claptrap, how many casks of sweetened pity liqueur (Firm: la religion de la souffrance), how many crutches of righteous indignation to prop up these flat-footed intellects, how many comedians of the Christian moral ideal would have to be exported from Europe today before its air smelled pure again. It is obvious that this over-production opens up a new trade possibility, and obvious that a new business is to be done in little ideal idols and obedient "idealists" — don't pass over this tip! Who has the courage? We hold in our hands the possibility of idealizing the whole earth. But what am I saying, courage? Here we need only one thing — a hand, a free, a very free hand.
